subject: sampling states in Hidden Markov models

messages.author: f778dcf899236084
messages.subject: sampling states in Hidden Markov models
parts:
Hi everybody,

I am playing around with hmm with continuous signals/observations. I implemented a hmm distribution like in the nimbleEcology package. Now I would like to sample from the hidden states (with the forward-backward algorithm).

My understading is that this is not implemented in the nimbleEcology package.

Any chance I can get intermediate values from the sampling process saved somehow (as in the "generated quantities" option of stan)? Or do I have to write a postprocessing script based on the posterior samples of the high-level parameters and implement this outside of the sampling?

Best,
Patrick

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: sampling states in Hidden Markov models
parts:
Short answer, Patrick: no, these quantities (samples of the intermediate latent states) are never themselves generated in the calculations done by the nimbleEcology distributions.  The latent states are marginalized over, by propagating a time-sequence of probabilities of each latent state value (at each time period), which are used to calculate the marginal probability of each data observation.

Given what you've said, I think your options are:
- Not use nimbleEcology, and write the latent states into your model, and thereby have samples of them.
- Write a post-processing script, as you mentioned, to generate the desired samples using the posterior samples of the model parameters.
- Modify one of the distributions in nimbleEcology, to use the intermediate probability values to also generate latent states.  Although, from the mechanics of how distributions work in NIMBLE, this would be somewhat awkward, and would (I believe) require you to further modify the model to imbed some of these probabilities (or their calculations) into the model itself, for the dual purpose of generating samples, and also calculating likelihoods.

That said, I may not be seeing all options clearly here, and hopefully others from the development team can also weigh in, with other ideas and options for you.

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: sampling states in Hidden Markov models
parts:
Great.  Now, you last question, user-defined distributions cannot and do not have "state" variables which can be set, and accessed later.  Samplers, on the other hand, can maintain state variables, which persist between sampling iteration.  So your best bet might be writing a custom sampler, adding it into the MCMC using 
mcmcConfigurationObject$addSampler(type = 'my_custom_sampler', ...)

and having this custom sampler maintain intermediate state variables (as necessary), and it could also access other nodes in the model, perform probability calculations, and even generate samples for latent states (using these probabilities, etc), and store them into a node(s) inside the model.  As for generating these samples during the course of the MCMC, this might be your best bet forward.  Otherwise, the post-processing script, as you've mentioned.

Cheers,
Daniel
